_readme: HAND-WRITTEN CEILINGS for the `context` gate. NO SCRIPT WRITES THIS FILE, and that is the
whole mechanism: harness-baseline.json — the other numbers file beside it — is rewritten in
full by an ordinary `node scripts/harness/measure-context.js` run, so a ceiling stored there
is one anybody lifts by running the routine command, with no deliberate re-baseline, no
refusal on a red, and no re-baseline commit subject. These numbers move only when a human
edits this file.
THE RULE: a ceiling is the measured byte count + 10%, rounded UP to the next 256 B. The
headroom is not slack, it is the thing that separates 'nobody did anything wrong' from
'someone spent past a declared budget'. An ordinary prose edit to a file measured by this rule
must not be able to red the suite; a pasted 600-byte block must. A row marked CARRIED OVER in
the working below was NOT measured by this rule and does not have that headroom yet: there, a
prose edit of a couple of hundred bytes reds the gate, and the fix is to re-measure the row.
Bytes are measured as git STORES the file: a CRLF pair is one byte. A checkout that converts
line endings therefore weighs exactly what the commit does, and the same commit cannot be
inside its ceiling on one machine and over it on another.
WHEN IT REDS: raise the number here, in the SAME commit as the growth, so the always-on cost
lands in that commit's diff. That is the only protocol. Do not re-record it somewhere else,
and do not reach for the gate runner's --accept — this file is not a gate figure and --accept
does not touch it.
SEMANTICS: a CEILING, one-sided. A row that shrank passes and prints its slack; a file deleted
from the tree passes; a `~/` row is the user's own config and is never graded; an UNTRACKED
file is never graded, because a red with no diff behind it cannot be fixed by editing a
tracked file. A tracked always-on file with NO entry here FAILS coverage — an unmeasured
always-on file must not pass silently. A bucket that holds ceilings here and graded NOTHING
fails for the same reason: a blind collector, or an empty git index, must not read as coverage.
WHERE THE ROWS COME FROM: `injected` is what the ENABLED tools load at session start, read
off each tool's policy route in scripts/harness/tools.json: the policy file, AGENTS.md, and for
a tool that reaches it through an import stub, the stub as well (CLAUDE.md). `nestedOnTouch`
is every other file of either name the measurement finds by WALKING the tree, so a new
subdirectory with its own instructions fails coverage the day it appears until someone budgets
it. `policyReads` is what only a LEAD opens: the routing doc under the docs root, plus every
root-level `.md` named in `docs.caps` in harness.config.json that no enabled tool injects —
writing a cap is how a repo declares a file worth a ceiling, so nothing here learns its name.
`generated` is for a file that is only PART authored. The agent-registry block between
<!-- agents:begin --> and <!-- agents:end --> in the routing doc is rewritten by
`node scripts/harness/docs-index.js --agents` from .claude/agents/*.md. So the ceiling above
grades the AUTHORED bytes only, and the block gets its own budget: baseBytes + bytesPerRow x
rows, with maxRows declaring how many rows this budget was written for. Adding an agent is
free; a bloated description is not; one agent past maxRows is a one-line edit here. Without
maxRows the derived total below would move with the tree, and a fixture that disagrees with
itself is what totalTokenCeiling exists to prevent. A row may also carry `beginMarker` and
`endMarker` when some other generator fences the block.
`totalTokenCeiling` is DERIVED, not chosen: tok(each injected + policyReads ceiling, plus its
generated allowance) + the LARGEST per-directory sum of tok(nestedOnTouch ceiling), at bytes/4,
mirroring the measurement's rule that a task touches one subtree, not all of them, and that one
touch loads every instruction file in that directory (a stub and the policy file it imports
arrive together). The gate recomputes it and
fails if this recorded figure disagrees, in EITHER direction, so the aggregate budget can never
contradict the per-row budgets it is made of. Recompute it whenever a ceiling changes:
`node scripts/harness/measure-context.js --self-test` prints both figures and says which.
NOT GRADED HERE, and named in the gate's own output every run so no green line stands in for
them: the `listing` bucket (skill, command and agent names and descriptions — third-party
bundles arrive untracked through an ordinary package command, so a ceiling would red on a file
nobody's diff would show), hook stdout, MCP tool definitions, and the per-subagent floor. The
generated doc index is measured, printed and deliberately absent from this file: nothing
injects it, and its size moves with every doc added or removed in the growth direction, so a
ceiling over it reds on commits where nobody did anything wrong.
THE FIGURES BELOW were measured against THIS repo's own files as they stood on 2026-10-05, by
the rule above — the working is kept here so the next edit can be checked rather than trusted:
AGENTS.md            5933 B measured            CARRIED OVER   -> 6144
CLAUDE.md            145 B measured (the stub)  -> 159.5  -> 256
templates/AGENTS.md  4034 B measured            -> 4437.4 -> 4608
templates/CLAUDE.md  145 B measured (the stub)  -> 159.5  -> 256
docs/reference/routing/README.md
8541 B, of which the generated block is 972 B over 4 rows,
so 7569 B authored         CARRIED OVER   -> 7680
generated block      190 B of fence and table header, rows of 188-205 B: 256 + 256 x rows
= 1600 + 2368 + 1216, the last term being templates/, both files
CARRIED OVER marks the two ceilings that were NOT recomputed by the rule. On 2026-10-05 the
policy body moved from CLAUDE.md into AGENTS.md and the routing body from AGENTS.md into the
routing doc, and each ceiling moved with its body: the move was not to buy either file one
byte. Both therefore hold less than 10% of slack (about 200 B and 100 B on that date), so the
headroom the rule promises is not there for these two. The next growth of either file
re-measures it by the rule, in the commit that grows it.
The two files under templates/ are starter files a new repo copies, and they are budgeted all
the same: the walk finds them, a tool that loads nested instruction files loads them when a
file under templates/ is touched, and a ceiling is what it costs to keep them in the tree.
A FRESH INSTALL does not get these figures. `harness init` writes its own copy of this file
with `"placeholder": true` at the top level and ceilings taken from the starter policy file,
stub and routing doc it has just rendered. The gate then prints a loud `!` line on every run and a pass
under it means little. Replace every figure with measured bytes + 10% rounded up, recompute
totalTokenCeiling, and delete the flag in the same commit.
